## Frozen commentary (Turkish)

On altıncı ve on yedinci ayetteki zaman kelimeleri, hareket halindeki bir at ya da deve dizisinde yer de bildirir. Birinci ayetteki tesbih fiilinin kökünde koşan at vardır: {ar:السابح من الخيل يمد يديه في الجري؛ النجوم تسبح في الفلك, tr:es-sâbihu mine'l-hayli yemuddu yedeyhi fi'l-cerî en-nucûmu tesbehu fi'l-felek, gloss:sâbih koşarken ön ayaklarını uzatan attır; yıldızlar yörüngelerinde yüzer, source:"س ب ح,B004"}. Kökün temel anlamı suda yüzmektir: {ar:سَبَحَ فِي ٱلْمَاءِ, tr:sebeha fi'l-mâ, gloss:suda yüzdü, source:"memory"}. Dizinin başında öncüler vardır: {ar:هوادي الخيل أعناقها أو أول رعيل, tr:hevâdi'l-hayli a'nâkuhâ ev evvelu racîl, gloss:atların hevâdîsi boyunlarıdır ya da ilk bölüktür, source:"ه د ي,B003"}. On beşinci ayetteki namaz kökü ikinci atı adlandırır: {ar:قد صلى وجاء مصليا لأن رأسه يتلو الصلا الذي بين يديه, tr:kad sallâ ve câe musalliyen li-enne ra'sehû yetlu's-salâ'lleẕî beyne yedeyh, gloss:musallî olarak geldi çünkü başı öndekinin sağrısını izler, source:"ص ل و,B006"}. {ar:السابق الأول والمصلي الثاني, tr:es-sâbiku'l-evvel ve'l-musallî es-ŝânî, gloss:sâbık birinci musallî ikincidir, source:"ص ل و,B006"}. Sekizinci ayetin kökü düzgün adımı verir: {ar:دابة حسن التيسور أي حسن نقل القوائم, tr:dâbbetun hasenu't-teysûr ey hasenu nakli'l-kavâim, gloss:ayaklarını güzel atan hayvan, source:"ي س ر,B005"}. On altıncı ayetteki tercih kökü, öne koymaktır: {ar:له أصل تقديم الشيء, tr:lehû aslu takdîmi'ş-şey', gloss:bir şeyi öne koyma anlamında bir kökü vardır, source:"ء ث ر,B001"}. Ama aynı kök birinin izinden gitmek de demektir: {ar:جاء فلان على إثري وأثري وجاء في أثره وإثره, tr:câe fulânun alâ isrî ve eserî ve câe fî eserihî ve isrih, gloss:falanca peşimden geldi; onun izinden geldi, source:"ء ث ر,B004"}. Dünya yakın kıyıdır: {ar:العدوة الدنيا والعدوة القصوى, tr:el-udvetu'd-dunyâ ve'l-udvetu'l-kusvâ, gloss:yakın yamaç ve uzak yamaç, source:"د ن و,B002"}. Ahiret kökü topluluğun arkasında kalanları adlandırır: {ar:أخرى القوم أي من كان في آخرهم, tr:uhra'l-kavmi ey men kâne fî âhirihim, gloss:topluluğun uhrâsı en arkada olandır, source:"ء خ ر,B001"}. Semerin arka direği de bu köktendir: {ar:آخرة الرحل وقادمته ومؤخر الرحل ومقدمه, tr:âhiratu'r-rahli ve kâdimetuhû ve muahharu'r-rahli ve mukaddemuh, gloss:semerin arka ve ön direği, source:"ء خ ر,B003"}. On yedinci ayetteki "kalıcı" kelimesinin ailesinde koşusunun bir kısmını saklayan atlar vardır: {ar:المبقيات من الخيل التي تبقي بعض جريها تدخره, tr:el-mubkıyâtu mine'l-hayli elletî tubkî ba'da cerîhâ teddehıruh, gloss:mubkıyât koşusunun bir kısmını saklayıp biriktiren atlardır, source:"ب ق ي,B004"}. On sekizinci ayetin "ilk" kelimesi de dizinin önündeki deveyi verir: {ar:ناقة أولة وجمل أول إذا تقدما الإبل, tr:nâkatun evvelatun ve cemelun evvelu iẕâ tekaddeme'l-ibil, gloss:develerin önüne geçen dişi deve ve erkek deve, source:"ء و ل,B001"}.

Bu dizi içinde on altıncı ve on yedinci ayet bir koşu olarak okunur. Öne koyduğunuz şey yakın olandır. Arkada gelen ise daha hayırlıdır ve daha uzun dayanır, tıpkı koşusunu sona saklayan at gibi. Düz bir anlatım yalnızca iki hayatı karşılaştırır. Bu sahne karşılaştırmaya bir zaman sırası ekler: ilk gelen yarışı kazanan değildir. On beşinci ayetteki "namaz kıldı" fiilinin ailesinde öncünün hemen ardından gelen ikinci at vardır. Bu, bir izleme hareketi olarak duyulur. Ama bu bağ kelimenin namaz anlamının yerine geçmez.

Kur'an yemin ettiği koşucularla bir sureyi açar: {ar:وَٱلسَّٰبِحَٰتِ سَبْحًۭا, tr:ve's-sâbihâti sebhâ, gloss:yüzdükçe yüzenlere andolsun, source:79:3}. Bu, Firavun'un "en yüce rabbinizim" dediği ve dünya hayatını tercih edenin anıldığı suredir. Bir başka yerde öndekiler {ar:وَٱلسَّٰبِقُونَ ٱلسَّٰبِقُونَ, tr:ve's-sâbikûne's-sâbikûn, gloss:öne geçenler ise öne geçenlerdir, source:56:10} diye anılır. Yakın ve uzak yamaç, iki topluluğun karşılaştığı günün tasvirinde geçer: {ar:إِذْ أَنتُم بِٱلْعُدْوَةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَهُم بِٱلْعُدْوَةِ ٱلْقُصْوَىٰ, tr:iẕ entum bi'l-udveti'd-dunyâ ve hum bi'l-udveti'l-kusvâ, gloss:o gün siz yakın yamaçtaydınız onlar uzak yamaçtaydı, source:8:42}. On altıncı ayetin cümle yapısı başka bir yerde neredeyse aynen tekrarlanır. Orada "yakın" yerine "acele gelen" kelimesi kullanılır: {ar:كَلَّا بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ, tr:kellâ bel tuhibbûne'l-âcile, gloss:hayır; siz acele geleni seviyorsunuz, source:75:20}, {ar:وَتَذَرُونَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ, tr:ve teẕerûne'l-âhira, gloss:ve sonra geleni bırakıyorsunuz, source:75:21}. Önce geleni tutup arkadan geleni bırakmak, bu dizideki yanlış sıralamadır.

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /Volumes/aro/projects/prose_generation/enrichment/bible/work/s087/discovery/prepared-20261005/sec15/luna/list.tsv
+strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.19.6	sun as runner on its course	The commentary extends 87:1's galloping-horse image to stars swimming in their courses; this psalm depicts the sun rejoicing like a champion to run its course, adding a celestial runner.
+medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.73.24	guidance now, glory afterward	The commentary joins 87:3's guidance to the later place in the procession; the psalm says God guides the speaker and afterward receives him to glory, making guidance lead toward a later reward.
+strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Exod.13.21	divine guide before the column	The commentary turns 87:3's guidance into vanguard leaders; Exodus says YHWH goes before Israel in cloud and fire to lead the route, giving guidance a literal front-of-column position.
+strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Exod.14.19	cloud shifts from front to rear	The commentary tracks leaders and those at the people's rear; as Egypt approaches, Exodus moves the divine messenger and cloud from before Israel to behind them, making the procession's order protective.
+strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Num.10.25	Dan as march rear guard	The commentary says the group's “after” names those at its end; Numbers assigns Dan's camp the rear guard for Israel's moving camps, a concrete final rank in the column.
+strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Josh.6.9	armed vanguard and rearguard	The commentary develops a front rank and followers behind; Joshua's Jericho procession places armed men before the priests and a rear guard behind the ark, adding a ritual march with both positions.
+strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.52.12	goes before and guards behind	The commentary maps first and last onto a moving line; Isaiah describes the departing people going without haste because YHWH goes before them and Israel's God is their rear guard.
+strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.58.8	righteousness before, glory behind	The commentary sets a leading rank against those at the rear; Isaiah promises healing with righteousness going before the people and YHWH's glory as their rear guard, giving the order a salvific meaning.
+strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Hab.3.15	horses in the sea	The commentary brings together swimming water and a running horse; Habakkuk's theophany has God tread the sea with horses, a concrete meeting of water and equine movement without equating their actions.
+medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.63.13	people led through depths like a sure-footed horse	The commentary praises an animal's well-placed steps and recalls swimming; Isaiah describes God leading Israel through depths like a horse in the wilderness that does not stumble, joining deep-water passage to sure-footed motion.
+strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.18.34	deer-like feet on high places	The commentary's yusr gloss depicts an animal transferring its legs well; the psalm says God makes the speaker's feet like a deer and sets him on high places, making sure-footed ascent a divine gift.
+medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Hab.3.19	hind's feet amid upheaval	The commentary reads 87:8's animal stride as well-placed movement; Habakkuk's prayer gives the speaker hind-like feet on high places amid crop failure and distress, adding sure footing as trust through crisis.
+medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.12.5	running with horses as endurance test	The commentary says the trailing horse has saved some running for later; Jeremiah's rebuke asks whether the prophet can contend with horses if footmen tire him, making endurance rather than an early lead the test.
+strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.9.11	race not decided by speed	The commentary says the first to arrive is not necessarily the winner; Ecclesiastes says the race is not to the swift and outcomes do not reliably follow strength or speed, directly unsettling rank by pace.
+medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:2Sam.18.23	Ahimaaz outruns the Cushite	The commentary distinguishes the first horse from the one following; Ahimaaz outruns the Cushite in a messenger race, supplying a narrative pair of first and trailing runners.
+medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:2Sam.18.29	first arrival lacks the decisive answer	The commentary warns that the first to arrive need not win; after outrunning the Cushite, Ahimaaz reaches David but cannot say what happened to Absalom, so speed does not deliver the needed result.
+medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:2Sam.18.32	later runner answers the king	The commentary says the one behind may matter more than the first; the Cushite arrives after Ahimaaz and answers David about Absalom, completing a messenger race in which the later report is decisive.
+medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.20.8	horses set against invoking God's name	The commentary pairs 87:15's remembering the Lord's name with horse imagery; this psalm contrasts trust in horses with invoking YHWH's name, adding a counterpoint in which the horse is inadequate as security.
+medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.119.32	running the way of commandments	The commentary couples guidance with an animal's ordered stride; the psalmist says he will run the way of God's commandments when his heart is enlarged, turning directed movement into obedience.
+medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.40.31	run without weariness	The commentary's horse saves part of its run for the later stretch; Isaiah promises that those who hope in YHWH will run without weariness, making sustained movement the result of renewed strength.
+strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Dan.2.23	Arabic source root س ب ح and Aramaic š-b-ḥ, praise	The commentary labels 87:1's Arabic root س ب ح and develops swimming and galloping associations; Daniel's Aramaic prayer uses the cognate root š-b-ḥ to praise God, grounding the worship sense without importing Daniel's word into the motion gloss.
+strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Dan.6.11	Arabic source root ص ل و and Aramaic ṣ-l-y, pray	The commentary labels 87:15 فَصَلَّى as prayer, then notes a second-horse sense in its lexical family; Daniel's Aramaic cognate describes his three daily prayers, anchoring the worship sense while leaving the horse image secondary.
+strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Eccl.7.8	Arabic source آخرة and Hebrew אחרית, latter end	The commentary says the Arabic “after/latter” root names those at the rear; Ecclesiastes uses the Hebrew cognate אחרית for a matter's end, and explicitly calls that end better than its beginning.
+strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.7.8	end better than beginning	The commentary says the later runner may be better than the first arrival; Ecclesiastes explicitly values a matter's end over its beginning, giving the temporal reversal a wisdom saying.
+medium	tevrat	motif	Mishnah Avot 4:16	vestibule before the World to Come	The commentary makes the nearer life the first part of a sequence and the afterlife the later part; Avot pictures this world as a vestibule before the World to Come, adding a preparatory threshold image.
+strong	tevrat	motif	Mishnah Avot 4:17	relative worth of the two worlds	The commentary calls the later life better and more enduring; Avot preserves both valuations: an hour of good deeds here exceeds the future world's whole life, yet an hour of its bliss exceeds all this world's life, complicating a simple ranking.
+medium	tevrat	motif	Mishnah Peah 1:1	fruit now, principal preserved for the World to Come	The commentary contrasts the near life with what remains afterward; Peah says some deeds bear fruit in this world while their principal remains for the World to Come, adding a specific image of reward held for later.
+medium	tevrat	motif	Wisdom.3.4	hope full of immortality	The commentary says the later life is more enduring than the present; Wisdom says the righteous dead seem destroyed to observers but have hope full of immortality, adding the hidden outcome behind apparent loss.
+medium	tevrat	motif	2Macc.7.9	present death accepted for resurrection	The commentary criticizes preferring the nearer life over what follows; the second Maccabean martyr refuses the king's offer and expects the King of the universe to raise him, presenting the contrary choice of future life over present survival.
+medium	tevrat	motif	2Macc.7.14	resurrection to life after death	The commentary calls the hereafter better and lasting; a brother facing execution says the dead will be raised to life, adding resurrection as the concrete future that makes present death bearable.
+strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.9.24	runners and the prize	The commentary distinguishes the leading and following horses and says early arrival is not the whole contest; Paul invokes runners in a stadium and urges the Corinthians to run to obtain the prize, making disciplined pursuit—not mere rank—the point.
+strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.9.25	imperishable crown	The commentary calls the later life more enduring and compares it to a horse saving its run; Paul contrasts athletes' perishable wreath with the imperishable one sought by Christians, joining race discipline to lasting reward.
+strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.12.1	run the set race with endurance	The commentary's final runner preserves strength for the later stretch; Hebrews tells its hearers to run the race set before them with endurance, making perseverance the necessary path to the finish.
+medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.12.2	joy set ahead of present suffering	The commentary values what comes later over the first arrival; Hebrews says Jesus endured the cross for the joy set before him and then sat at God's right hand, giving present suffering a future-directed end.
+medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Phil.3.13	reaching toward what lies ahead	The commentary's race image turns the two lives into first and later positions; Paul says he forgets what lies behind and reaches toward what lies ahead, making forward orientation the posture of pursuit.
